title: Two population pyramids: Niger and Japan
examples: Why does Niger have so many young people?

explain.say: Imagine lining up everyone in a country by age: babies at the bottom, grandparents at the top, boys on one side, girls on the other. The shape you get is called a population pyramid. Look at the board: two countries with very different shapes.

draw.text: Two population pyramids: Niger and Japan

draw.name: x-compare

left.title: Niger
left.ask: Why does Niger have so many young people?

draw.verdict: The shape tells the story of births, deaths and age

explain.say: Look at Niger, in West Africa. Its pyramid has a very wide base, which means lots of children. About half of all people there are under 15, and women have about six children on average. Fewer people reach old age, so the sides slope in fast. Can you picture a tall triangle?

draw.name: x-compare

left.title: Niger
left.ask: Why does Niger have so many young people?

draw.verdict: The shape tells the story of births, deaths and age

explain.say: Now Japan. The base is narrow, because few babies are born, about 1.2 per woman. But the top is wide: almost 3 in every 10 people are 65 or older, and many live past 90. It looks more like a vase than a pyramid. Can you see why it is called top-heavy?

draw.verdict: The shape tells the story of births, deaths and age

explain.say: Each shape brings its own challenges. Look at the two groups. A young country like Niger needs more schools, jobs for young people and health care for children. An ageing country like Japan needs care for older people and has fewer workers. Which challenge seems hardest to you?

groups.ask: What problems does an ageing population bring?

explain.say: So a pyramid is like a photo of a country’s past and future. Excellent thinking! Wow fact: in Japan, more adult nappies are now sold than baby nappies, a sign of how the population is ageing.

faq.a: A population pyramid is a bar chart of a country’s people by age group, with males on one side and females on the other, youngest at the bottom. Its shape shows birth rates, death rates and how long people live.
asks: How do you read a population pyramid?

faq.q: Why does Niger have so many young people?
faq.a: Women in Niger have about six children on average, one of the highest rates in the world. Many families farm and rely on children’s help, many girls marry young, and fewer girls stay in school.
asks: Why do women in Niger have many children?

faq.a: Few babies are born in Japan, about 1.2 per woman, and people live very long, about 84 years on average. Few people move to Japan from abroad, so the population is getting older and smaller.

faq.q: What problems does an ageing population bring?
faq.a: There are fewer workers to keep the economy going and pay taxes, while more older people need pensions and health care. Japan is trying robots, later retirement and more workers from abroad.
asks: How is Japan dealing with an ageing population?

faq.a: It compares the number of children under 15 and older people over 64 with the number of working-age people, 15 to 64. Both Niger and Japan have many dependants, but for opposite reasons.
asks: Who are dependants in a population?

facts: Niger has one of the youngest populations in the world, with a median age of about 15.
In 2023 about 29% of Japan's people were aged 65 or over.
Japan's fertility rate was about 1.2 children per woman in 2023, among the lowest in the world.

quiz.say: A pyramid has a very wide base and a narrow top. What does that tell you?
quiz.show: A wide base and narrow top means…

options.show: Many children and fewer older people
options.say: Many children and fewer older people

options.show: Many older people and few children
options.say: Many older people and few children

quiz.why: The base shows the youngest people, so a wide base means many children.

wrong.1: Many older people would make the top wide, like Japan.
wrong.2: If everyone were the same age, there would be just one wide bar.

quiz.say: Which challenge comes with an ageing population like Japan's?

options.show: Fewer workers and more people needing care
options.say: Fewer workers and more people needing care

options.show: Too many new schools to build
options.say: Too many new schools to build

quiz.why: With few young people and many older ones, there are fewer workers and more people needing care and pensions.

wrong.1: Needing many new schools is a challenge for young countries like Niger.
wrong.2: Fewer babies means less need for baby clothes, not a shortage.
